Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature — Thu Aug 6 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: "Myths are the world's dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment — Thu Aug 6 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Momentexamines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?This exhibition is part of America 250 at IU (

item.title: McCalla Open Gallery Hours — Thu Aug 6, 11:00 AM — McCalla Building
item.description: Outfitting IU Athletics: Hoosier Champions This exhibit showcases objects from IU's championship teams and athletes, connecting them to historic achievements in the Big Ten and the national stage. The items featured in the exhibit are from the IU Athletics Sports Memorabilia Collection and feature photos and videos provided by IU Athletics and Indiana University Archives. Dates: November 14, 2025 - October 2026 By Their Own Hands: The Black Filmmakers Hall of Fame! Founded in 1974 by the Culture and Ethnic Affairs Guild of the Oakland Museum of California, the Black Filmmakers Hall of Fame began as a film lecture series and awards ceremony celebrating achievements of Black film industry figures. When that organization closed, they donated their materials to IU. In collaboration with the IU Black Film Center and Archive, this exhibit features objects from that collection, including founding documents, costumes

item.title: West Baden Hoosier Masters Paint-Out — Fri Aug 7, 12:00 PM — One Artist Drive. Nashville
item.description:
This weekend, Indiana artists will gather at the beautiful West Baden Springs Hotel to paint and exhibit their work on the historic grounds. Artists from across the state, along with local residents and hotel guests, will enjoy this unique event, making it a wonderful opportunity to experience Indiana art in an unforgettable setting. Artists will display paintings created during the event beneath the hotel’s magnificent dome during a Saturday afternoon reception featuring food and beverages. The hotel actively promotes the event to its guests and even purchases artwork each year.
Source: Brown County Events

item.title: Steve Hickman — Sat Aug 8, 1:30 PM — Ferguson House Beer Garden
Aaron Grubb — Sat Aug 8, 2:00 PM — Moontown Brewing Co.
Artist Talk and Demonstration Catherine Baum-Newlin — Sat Aug 8, 2:00 PM — Juniper Art Gallery
item.description:
Please join us for a creative Saturday afternoon with local artist, Catherine Baum-Newlin. She will give a demonstration and take your questions while we watch her create!
The Artist will share what best illustrates a process of ‘creating’ that she finds helpful.
She says, “Art practice is like practicing my violin, fast writes in writing practice, or showing up to meditate. First, just show up and be present. Next, ‘play’ comes along with elements of curiosity, noticing, and observing. ‘Allowing’ enters and, with that, a deeper ‘you’ shows up. Thoughts, sounds, words, images are present. Good or bad becomes irrelevant. I almost always feel I’m learning.”
In the demo, she will do a ‘play’ page in her notebook, paint some washi papers, make some marks and we’ll see what happens! This is sure to be an experimental, fun, and playful afternoon!
Source: Pillar Arts Community Calendar

item.title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature — Sat Aug 15 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: "Myths are the world's dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment — Sat Aug 15 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Momentexamines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain?
